answers.how: From the given depth info at t=1.0s (151.1 cm) and t=1.4s (103.0 cm), the displacement over the 0.4s interval centered at t=1.2s is 48.1 cm, giving a midpoint velocity of 48.1 / 0.4 = 120.25 cm/s (and ~125 cm/s from local projective tracking of the ball between Frames 26 and 31).

Tracking the ball's contact point and apparent diameter across Frames 32 (t=1.333s, Z=107.2 cm) to 36 (t=1.500s, Z=91.7 cm) calibrated with Z=103.0 cm at t=1.4s gives an instantaneous velocity around t=1.4s of approximately 95-105 cm/s.

Calibrating focal length from the 40 mm ping pong ball at the given depths (f ≈ 484 px at 853x480 resolution) and measuring the table's horizontal width of 188.7 px at the t=1.0s ball depth (151.1 cm) yields W = 188.7 * 151.1 / 484 ≈ 59.5 cm.

From the perspective foreshortening of the table edges (back edge 181.5 px at Z_back ≈ 159.0 cm, front edge 333.0 px at Z_front ≈ 86.5 cm), the table length from back to front is 159.0 - 86.5 = 72.5 cm.
